caveats: ADV-C2 compares en and th and requires every screens leaf to differ. No exception was needed. Spec 6.3 creates no en/th equality. The only spec-sanctioned cross-locale equality is D-10 (zh equals en), which ADV-C3 asserts, so an untranslated zh placeholder is the intended state and not a defect.

ADV-C4 searches the whole locale file with raw substring inclusion and no line filter, so a retired line beside 'do not' or 'never' is still caught. The positive-control assertions prove the predicate fires.
A9 check: no new test reads a measure/tracks, measure/runs, or measure/archive path. The source scan in ADV-G5 reads only files under the app's src directory.
n1_judgement: Review C's N1 describes a real visual effect: at viewports of 1169 px and above a phone card renders about 576 CSS px wide against a 520 px source, so the browser upscales roughly 11 percent. This is not a sharpness defect that a test or a copy change must fix. Spec D-14 states a vitest cannot read pixels, and 520 px is the largest delivered phone source, so no code change here can add detail. Spec open question 6 and test-strategy section 8.1 record that Daniel accepts the softness or PR captures again. N1 is therefore a page-check judgement for the PM in task 2.5, or an owner decision to recapture. No Playwright sharpness test was added.
